newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur barges up, straight-run slips bac.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur barges up, straight-run slips bac.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel barges picked up on Wednesday, gaining support from bunker demand and general strength in the product market, traders said.
Offers rose to $87 fob ARA by late morning, up $2 on yesterday, with earlier trades at $85.50 fob for second half April delivery. Trades were also seen at $86.
Bunker demand was moderate. Traders said values for Mediterranean high sulphur cargoes were being bid higher for pricing purposes, lending some support to the North.
Most other oil products were gaining on the back of the recovery in IPE Brent and gas oil futures.
Low sulphur cracked was expected to come under pressure from straight-run, which continues to be chronically weak.

Offers for straight-run were heard at $95 fob, with good mid-April availability. One 30,000 tonne cargo of straight-run was heard traded at $95 fob on Monday from the UK to southern France, but this could not be confirmed.
